findings.reason: the section must exempt the synthesized keys or name their origin explicitly; otherwise a worker on an exact spec either fails its own gate or fabricates a source for keys that have none.
findings.text: §9's done-when requires "every key of both entries" to carry a provenance record naming the `lanes.*` key it came from, but `_lane_entry` (reckon/flight.py:1320) writes three keys — `lane`, `model_key`, `derived_from` — that are synthesized by the expansion and read from no `lanes.*` key, so those keys cannot satisfy a source-naming record and a test written to the done-when as stated cannot pass

findings.reason: without a stated shape the worker either drops the source-key half of the requirement or changes a contract that callers outside the write path depend on, and either outcome is the node deciding a question the plan left open.
findings.text: §9's done-when requires each provenance record to name the source `lanes.*` key *and* "the layer it was read from", two facts, but the resolver's provenance is `dict[str, str]` mapping a key path to a bare layer name (`ResolvedFlight.provenance`, reckon/flight.py:175), exposed through `origin()` and asserted as `== "<layer>"` by `.origin()` calls across ~10 test files outside §9's write paths, so the record cannot carry both facts without a value-shape change §9 does not declare
